intro.label: Before Puppy Comes Home
intro.heading: Griffon Puppy Prep: Health Documentation and Exercise Planning
intro.html:
Before your Wirehaired Pointing Griffon puppy arrives, confirm OFA hip and CAER eye documentation from both parents, enroll in pet insurance before the first vet visit, and plan for the exercise and mental engagement this active working breed requires from early in life.

This guide contains affiliate links. As an Amazon Associate, Wooffy earns from qualifying purchases.

Health Documentation to Confirm Before Purchase

  • OFA hip certification for both parents — hip dysplasia is the primary orthopedic risk for this breed
  • CAER ophthalmology exam for both parents
  • Elbow certification if available

Essential Gear Checklist

  • Large crate (36–42 inch with divider for growth)
  • Orthopedic dog bed
  • Stainless steel bowls
  • Flat collar + ID tag (engrave immediately on arrival)
    One option: GoTags Personalized Stainless Steel ID Tag on Amazon. An engraved stainless steel ID tag; you pick the shape and the lines of text at checkout. Put a phone number that's actually answered on it, and update the engraving if you move.
  • Harness for walks
  • 4–6 ft leash and 20–30 ft long line for recall work in open areas
    One option: Joytale Double-Handle Leash (6 ft) on Amazon. A 6-foot nylon leash with a padded second handle near the clip for close control, plus reflective stitching for dark walks. The 1-inch webbing suits medium and large dogs; it can feel heavy on a young puppy.
  • Slicker brush and wide-tooth metal comb
    One option: Chris Christensen Big G Slicker Brush on Amazon. Long angled pins in a flexible cushioned pad that lift dead hair and work through leg and beard furnishings. Use light strokes; slicker pins can scratch skin if pressed hard.
  • Veterinary ear cleaning solution and cotton balls
    One option: Virbac Epi-Otic Advanced Ear Cleanser on Amazon. A gentle, low-pH, alcohol-free ear cleanser made for routine cleaning and drying of the ear canal. Routine cleaning only; if the ear is red, smelly or painful, see your vet before putting anything in it.
  • High-value training treats
    One option: Blue Buffalo Bits Soft Training Treats, Beef (19 oz) on Amazon. Soft, bite-size training treats with real beef as the first ingredient, small enough for rapid repetitions. Keep treats to about 10% of daily calories.
  • Bird-scented training dummies if field work is planned
  • Durable chew toys
  • Enzymatic cleaner
    One option: Rocco & Roxie Enzyme Stain & Odor Eliminator (32 oz) on Amazon. An enzyme stain and odor eliminator for urine, feces and vomit, carrying the Carpet and Rug Institute's seal for carpets. Spot-test on delicate fabrics first.

care.label: First Week Priorities
care.heading: First Vet Visit and Early Routines
care.html:
Insurance Before the First Vet Visit

Enroll in pet insurance on arrival day, before the puppy's first veterinary appointment. For the Griffon, orthopedic coverage is the priority — hip dysplasia surgery at $3,500–$7,000 per hip is the most significant potential cost. Enrolling before the first vet visit preserves the broadest possible coverage for conditions that may develop later.

First Vet Visit (Within 48–72 Hours)

  • Full physical exam
  • Vaccine schedule verification and continuation
  • Parasite prevention discussion
  • Discuss spay/neuter timing — for medium-to-large sporting breeds, some evidence supports 18–24 months for full musculoskeletal development before altering
  • Eye exam and baseline documentation
  • Microchip if not done by breeder

Starting the Ear and Grooming Routine

Begin weekly ear cleaning and brushing from the first week. The Griffon's pendant ears require consistent cleaning, especially if water work is planned. The beard and eyebrows need weekly combing to prevent mat formation and debris accumulation. Establishing grooming tolerance from puppyhood makes adult maintenance straightforward.

special.label: Field Exposure and Socialization
special.heading: Field Exposure and Socialization for Griffon Puppies
special.html:
Socialization Window: 8–16 Weeks

Wirehaired Pointing Griffons are people-oriented dogs that generally socialize readily. Active socialization during the critical window builds a confident, adaptable adult. Prioritize:

  • Varied people — different ages, appearances, children, field companions
  • Novel environments — different terrains, weather conditions, urban and rural settings
  • Controlled dog interactions through puppy classes
  • Handling: ears, paws, beard area, coat — all areas that require regular maintenance

Field Exposure — Start Early for Hunting Dogs

For owners planning hunting work, early exposure to birds and field conditions makes a significant difference in how the dog develops. Griffon puppies as young as 8–12 weeks can be introduced to bird scent through feathers or frozen birds in low-pressure, positive sessions. By 4–6 months, light field exposure — walking through bird cover, brief contacts with live or frozen birds — begins developing the instincts the breed carries. This is not formal training; it is exposure that supports the natural ability.

Formal pointing and hunting dog training typically begins at 6–8 months. Identify a bird dog trainer experienced with Griffons or continental pointing breeds before the puppy is ready — good trainers have wait lists.

Exercise Planning

Adult Griffons need 60–90 minutes of vigorous exercise daily. For puppies, this builds gradually — short walks, play sessions, and field exposure with rest periods for the first 12 months. The breed's energy is substantial; owners who plan adequately for exercise commitment find them manageable and pleasant companions. Those who don't find an entirely different experience.

faq.q: Do I need to hunt to own a Wirehaired Pointing Griffon?
faq.a: No — but you need to provide the exercise and mental engagement that hunting naturally supplies. A Griffon kept as a companion dog without field work needs an equivalent outlet: vigorous daily exercise, nose work or tracking activities, hunt test participation, or other structured activity. The breed's drive and energy are real. Without adequate outlets, they become destructive and difficult. With adequate outlets, they are excellent, adaptable family dogs.

faq.q: At what age should I start training a Wirehaired Pointing Griffon?
faq.a: Basic obedience (sit, down, stay, come, leash walking) starts from the first week at home. Bird and field exposure for hunting-intent owners begins as early as 8–12 weeks informally. Formal hunting dog training — steadiness, quartering, pointing, retrieving — typically begins at 6–8 months when drive and attention span are developing. Early informal field exposure before formal training is beneficial, not a substitute for it.

faq.q: How do I find a Wirehaired Pointing Griffon breeder?
faq.a: The American Wirehaired Pointing Griffon Association (AWPGA) maintains a breeder referral list and health testing standards for the breed. Because Griffons are relatively uncommon outside hunting dog circles, wait times for puppies from health-testing breeders are common. Plan 6–12 months ahead. Attend AWPGA events or regional breed club events where you can meet breeders and adult dogs before committing.
